A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnesSuite/Morpheus work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained equations, figures, tables, and analyses can be matched despite renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM evaluations on AnesBench, Morpheus training results, ablations, contamination analyses, and supplementary evaluations, including Tables 3–5 and Appendices A–G.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds Morpheus-32B, additional training experiments, training-reward curves, and evaluations on six broader benchmarks.

M1.justification: The new Morpheus-32B uses a LoRA training adaptation (Appendix C.2), introducing a limited change in trainable parameterization. The dataset-construction procedures and SFT-then-GRPO pipeline are retained. Newly specifying the binary reward does not establish that the existing reward mechanism changed.

E1.justification: New Appendix G.1 evaluates MedQA, MedMCQA, MedExpQA, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, and AGIeval, extending coverage from anesthesiology to broader medical and general-domain tasks. MedExpQA adds French, Italian, and Spanish evaluation, while MedQA includes Mainland, Taiwan, and US subsets. The earlier CAB, translated AnesBench, and open-ended evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to the direct Morpheus comparison, although it already appeared in v2's broader evaluations. New Table 11 compares AnesR1-trained Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma2-2B, and Gemma3-4B against their instruction-tuned controls. The main benchmark comparator roster in Tables 3 and 9 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported SFT-only control from models trained for an equivalent number of steps to intermediate cold-start checkpoints, materially changing the stated comparison design. v3 also adds the 32B configuration, 200-step Llama/Gemma training experiments, and an AGIeval protocol restricted to 18 MCQ tasks. Retained scores are unchanged, so the control-description revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G.1 adds substantial distribution-shift testing of whether anesthesiology training transfers to other medical and general domains, with language and task breakdowns. Appendix C.2 adds training-stability curves and tests AnesR1 effectiveness on additional model backbones. Existing contamination, scaling, translation, CPT/data ablations, self-consistency, and clinical case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 first reports three independent Morpheus-7B training runs and displays their mean reward with a one-standard-deviation band in Figure 9. Figure 10 shows a 14B reward curve without corresponding uncertainty reporting. Existing bootstrap confidence intervals, significance tests, and repeated open-ended judging remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an increase from a previously specified training-run count.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation results are retained, while Table 4 adds Morpheus-32B results, Table 11 adds training comparisons, and Tables 17–22 add extensive generalization results. For example, the new MMLU comparison reports 0.786 for Morpheus-7B versus 0.709 for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Gains are not universal: Table 18 reports Italian accuracy of 0.464 versus 0.512, and Table 22 shows engineering declines at all three Morpheus sizes.

T1.justification: The contamination confidence-score definition in Equation 1 and the regression model and associated mathematical reasoning in Equation 2 are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction, contribution statement, and conclusion broaden Morpheus's claimed benefits from anesthesiology performance to consistent improvements across anesthesiology, general medical, and general-domain benchmarks. This substantially expands the claimed scope of specialized reasoning-data training. The abstract and original dataset-suite contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix G.1 interprets the added results as cross-domain and cross-lingual reasoning transfer and attributes gains to better use of existing knowledge because training was confined to anesthesiology. Appendix C.2 also adds interpretations concerning training stability and Qwen-specific sensitivity after SFT. Existing limitations concerning abstract clinical scenarios and missing modalities remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly documents the binary correctness reward and regular-expression answer extraction, plus Morpheus-32B's LoRA rank 128, scaling factor 32, and 50 GRPO steps. It also reports the additional experiments' 200-step budget. Existing hardware, software, principal training hyperparameters, and promised code/data release arrangements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MedExpQA, MedQA, MedMCQA, MMLU-Pro, and AGIeval, plus Cheng et al. (2025) on cross-domain reasoning. It positions transfer from a small, specialized source domain relative to that generalization literature. The dedicated related-work sections are otherwise substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to the introduction, contribution statement, Section 4.2, and conclusion, with explanatory additions in Appendix C.2 and a new Appendix G.1 subsection. The overall section order and most prose remain intact. Header capitalization and appendix cross-references are also updated.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the empirical displays with GRPO reward curves, including variability shading, an additional-training table, and benchmark, language, and subject breakdown tables. Table 4 gains the 32B comparison and 72B control, and Figure 1 includes Morpheus-32B. Existing plots are retained, with several figures and tables relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The transfer evaluations and training-stability evidence address questions left untested in v2, while explicit reward and LoRA details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the revised SFT-control description and an unsupported reasoning-only causal attribution in Appendix G.1. New baseline values also remain unreconciled: Qwen2.5-72B English accuracy is 0.65 in Table 4 versus 0.67 in Table 9, and Gemma3-4B is 0.32 in Table 11 versus 0.42 in Table 9. Broader evidence and clearer documentation provide a limited net improvement.
